clue.text: Economist giving course for cannibals?

definitions.meaning: Milton ... was the American monetarist economist
a dish of cooked human being, a man that has been fried, is what a cannibal might serve as a course

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which economist would suit a cannibal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Friedman, the Chicago monetarist, is among the best-known twentieth-century economists.

clue.text: Do without fine herb-article to be avoided

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: to be avoided means the article is dropped from the herb

parts.note: oregano is a culinary herb
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: skip a good herb, and leave out an item too.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego something is to go without it, give it up.

clue.text: Denied falsely or truly

indicators.note: falsely suggests the letters are set out wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Was it denied in falsehood, or in truth?
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb of emphasis meaning really or in fact.

clue.text: Free church official rejecting a fish without its tail

indicators.note: rejecting means the church official throws out the letter named

parts.note: a deacon is a church officer

indicators.note: without its tail drops the last letter of the fishing word

parts.note: to troll is to fish by trailing a line

explanation.surface: A liberated churchman who turns down a fish lacking its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun, but it is the verb TROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To decontrol is to release from controls, set free of regulation.

clue.text: Agitated cockney greeting old man? Police officer must intervene

parts.note: a Londoner's dropped-aitch hello, written with the H gone

indicators.note: must intervene means the officer goes inside the old man

parts.note: old man is slang for one's father
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: An excited Londoner says hello to dad, and a policeman has to step in.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney (a working-class Londoner) drops the H of hello.
explanation.definitionFit: All of a dither is an idiom for being in a nervous, flustered state.

clue.text: Party leader at first exploits advantages

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the two words Party and leader

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it, so exploits gives uses

explanation.surface: A party chief who begins by making the most of every edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' looks like one person, but 'at first' takes the opening letters of both words, P and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluses are plus points, favourable features, so the plural noun means good points or benefits.

clue.text: Hem in 12, not quite the thing

indicators.note: not quite means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: 12-across is a colour, and lime is a shade of it
it can stand for the thing in question

explanation.surface: Sewing advice: the hem nearly matches but is not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' points to the answer of 12-across, a colour, and LIME is a shade of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit is to restrict or confine, as hedging something in does.

clue.text: Describing some languages wrongly could be vocal sin

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A remark about languages that could be a sin of speech if put badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavonic is the adjective for the Slavic language family, such as Russian and Polish.

clue.text: Locum with grand reputation

parts.note: a locum is a stand-in for a doctor or cleric
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A temporary doctor with an excellent name.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing means status or repute in the eyes of others.

clue.text: Law broken by one detective knocking off last guy

indicators.note: a word broken by others has them set inside it, splitting it

parts.note: a rule is a law
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: knocking off the last letter removes the end of the word for a detective

parts.note: dick is slang for a detective

explanation.surface: A rule bent by a lone sleuth who bumps off the final man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' reads as a man but is the verb: to guy someone is to mock them.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy is an old verb meaning to make fun of or mock, the same as to deride.

clue.text: Almost spear a beast

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to spear something is to impale it

explanation.surface: Someone nearly runs an animal through with a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Road up under plane tree

indicators.note: under places the road after the plane in this down entry

parts.note: the Wellington was a British wartime bomber aircraft

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters climb, read backwards

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's main north-south road, written with I for the figure 1

explanation.surface: Climbing the road under a plane tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane tree' looks like one tree; plane is the bomber and tree alone is the definition. The A1 is the trunk road from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellingtonia is the British name for the giant sequoia, a huge conifer.

clue.text: Party label one may be putting on

definitions.meaning: the name of the environmentalist political party, worn as a label
a golf putting surface, where a player putts

explanation.surface: A political badge someone might be pinning on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Party bears that colour name, and a golf course has a smooth lawn where players putt.

clue.text: Possibly deal with ships first in fishing port

indicators.note: first places the ships before the timber in the answer

parts.note: a fleet is a group of ships
deal is a kind of softwood timber, so possibly deal is an example of wood

explanation.surface: A trading arrangement with shipping as the priority in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a trade agreement but is pine or fir timber, hence 'Possibly'. FLEETWOOD is a fishing port in Lancashire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleetwood is a Lancashire coastal town long known for its trawler fleet and fish docks.

clue.text: Liking life, but not if involved in fortune-telling

indicators.note: involved in means set inside the other word

parts.note: telling fortunes is predicting, a prediction

indicators.note: but not removes the named letters from the word life

explanation.surface: Someone fond of life who wants no conditions in a fortune-teller's reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life' reads as part of the surface sense of fondness, but it is the raw material; 'involved in' then buries what remains inside the seer's forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A predilection is a preference or partiality, a fondness for something.

clue.text: Supported by female, scout must be prepared as usual

indicators.note: in a down entry, supported by puts the girl's name beneath
must be prepared plays on the Scout motto, and signals the letters are reworked

parts.note: Mary is a typical female name

explanation.surface: A scout, backed by a woman, must be ready as ever, as the motto says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be prepared' is the Scout motto, so the clue's surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary means usual or habitual, according to custom.

clue.text: Go in to sunder girl and boy, not weakening

indicators.note: to sunder is to split apart, so the batting goes between the two names

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
Ed is a boy's name
to go in, at cricket, is to bat

explanation.surface: Someone stepping in to part a girl and boy, with undiminished vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to go in is to take one's turn batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabated means without any lessening in force or intensity.

clue.text: Get-together excluding first person was first to be designated thus

indicators.note: excluding means the first person is left out of the gathering

parts.note: a social is a party, a get-together
I is the first person pronoun
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A party leaving out the first guest, who had arrived first.
explanation.definitionFit: So-called means named in that way, often implying doubt about the name.

clue.text: Philosophy from which ample notions may be derived

indicators.note: may be derived says the answer can be worked out of these letters by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A school of thought that could yield plentiful ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints the follower's word, ending -IST, but the fodder and the definition both give the doctrine ending -ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoplatonism is the mystical school of thought founded by Plotinus, reviving Plato's ideas.

clue.text: Musical setting has good old-fashioned look — setting for lark ascending?

parts.note: lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look

indicators.note: ascending in a down clue means the letters run upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lark rises and sings in the air

explanation.surface: A tune with a pleasing old look, set for The Lark Ascending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Lark Ascending' is a piece by Vaughan Williams; here the air, the lark's home, is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gloria is a hymn of the Mass that composers set to music.

clue.text: Spanner required for game

definitions.meaning: something spanning a gap, as a river crossing does
the card game for four players in pairs

explanation.definitionFit: A bridge spans a river, and bridge is also a trick-taking card game.

clue.text: Combatant who's qualified to make jet fly

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
to belt along is to fly, go very fast

explanation.surface: A fighter skilled enough to get an aircraft airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' and 'fly' suggest aircraft, but jet is the colour and fly means race along.
explanation.definitionFit: A black belt is the top grade in judo or karate, held by a fully qualified fighter.

clue.text: Bag containing right seafood

indicators.note: containing means the letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: to bag game is to kill it

explanation.surface: A sack holding the proper shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag' looks like a sack but is the hunter's verb, to shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny marine crustaceans, eaten by whales and sometimes people.

clue.text: Labourer scratching his head in tanker

indicators.note: scratching his head removes the first letter of the word for a worker

parts.note: one who toils is a toiler, a labourer

explanation.surface: A puzzled worker on board an oil ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching his head' looks like puzzlement but means striking off the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a ship that carries oil, a tanker, especially one refuelling naval vessels.

clue.text: Story about the King and I may be a Hollywood production

indicators.note: about means placed round the other letters

parts.note: a tale is a story
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A tale about the musical The King and I, which was filmed in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' looks like the musical's title, but it is split into K and I, put inside TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkie is an early film with a soundtrack, a motion picture of the kind Hollywood made.

clue.text: Not injured if pitching underarm

indicators.note: pitching suggests a throw, signalling the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A bowler or pitcher kept safe by throwing underarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarred means unspoiled, without damage or blemish.

clue.text: Benefit when theologian's swallowed piece of cake

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside the other word

parts.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar who gobbles a slice of cake while on welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the British slang name for state unemployment payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddle is British slang for something very easy, just as a piece of cake is.

clue.text: Retired sailor next to confront smoothie

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the sailor's letters run backwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
by means beside, next to
to face someone is to confront them

explanation.surface: An old seaman squares up to a slick charmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a suave, smooth-faced person, and a babyface has the smooth looks of an infant.
